description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:109-120:

    pub use pkix_aia::{self, AiaError, AiaFetcher, NoAiaFetcher};
    pub use pkix_identity::{self, IdentityError, MailboxName, ServerName};
    pub use pkix_path::{
        self, DefaultVerifier, Profile, SignatureVerifier, TrustAnchor, ValidatedPath, ValidationPolicy,
    };
    pub use pkix_revocation::{self, NoRevocation, RevocationChecker};

The `self` re-exports — `pub use pkix_aia`, `pub use pkix_identity`, `pub use pkix_path`, `pub use pkix_revocation` — re-publish each upstream crate's ENTIRE public surface under `pkix_chain::*`. A caller can write:

    pkix_chain::pkix_aia::HttpFetcher
    pkix_chain::pkix_path::validate_path_with_profile
    pkix_chain::pkix_revocation::ocsp::OcspResponse

…and depend on every symbol those crates export.

WHY IT MATTERS:

The slash-command checklist for versioning calls out:

> Re-exports from upstream crates that lock the major version. If you `pub use foo::Bar` and `foo` cuts a major version, your crate's API is broken too. Either re-export through your own newtype or document the upstream version pin.

With `pub use pkix_aia::{self, ...}` the re-export is BROADER than the checklist scenario: pkix-chain is locked to the entire surface of pkix-aia, not just AiaError/AiaFetcher/NoAiaFetcher. Every breaking change in pkix-aia transitively breaks pkix-chain — even changes to types pkix-chain does not itself consume.

Concrete scenarios where the lock-in fires:

1. pkix-aia 0.2.0 renames a non-AIA-trait type (say, an internal `AiaCacheKey` becomes `AiaCacheId`). The module-level re-export means pkix-chain consumers who reached through `pkix_chain::pkix_aia::AiaCacheKey` now have a broken import. Even though pkix-chain itself doesn't use this type.

2. pkix-revocation 0.4.0 changes the `ocsp` submodule layout. pkix-chain consumers reaching through `pkix_chain::pkix_revocation::ocsp::*` now have broken imports. pkix-chain has no use of those internals but is implicated in the break.

3. The MSRV-bump scenario: pkix-aia raises rust-version to 1.80 to use a stable-only feature. pkix-chain's MSRV (currently 1.73) is force-bumped because of the transitive module re-export — even if pkix-chain itself uses no 1.80 features.

The Cargo.toml line 4 already acknowledges the cost ("transitively breaking: pkix-path 0.3 ValidatedPath re-export"). That comment captures awareness of the issue for ValidatedPath specifically; the broader `pub use pkix_path::{self, ...}` extends the same risk to everything in pkix-path.

OPTIONS:

(a) **Drop the `self` re-exports.** Keep the named-symbol re-exports (`AiaError`, `AiaFetcher`, …) but remove `pub use pkix_aia` (the crate module). Callers who genuinely need the full upstream API import the upstream crate directly, with their own version pin. pkix-chain's API surface becomes "only the named symbols we use."

(b) **Newtype the upstream types** pkix-chain consumes directly (TrustAnchor, ValidationPolicy, ValidatedPath, etc.). This breaks the zero-cost identity between pkix_chain::TrustAnchor and pkix_path::TrustAnchor (a constraint the test `default_verifier_reexport_type_identity` lines 1668-1673 already pins), so it's the heavyweight option.

(c) **Document the version-pin contract**: a rustdoc paragraph at the top of lib.rs explicitly says "pkix-chain MAJOR version follows pkix-path / pkix-aia / pkix-revocation / pkix-identity — any major bump in those crates triggers a pkix-chain major bump." This makes the lock-in legible to consumers but does not remove it.

The current CHANGELOG header (line 4: "transitively breaking") already implies (c) is operative for pkix-path's ValidatedPath. Extending the same documented pin to pkix-aia, pkix-revocation, pkix-identity makes the contract explicit; dropping the `self` re-exports per (a) makes the lock-in much narrower at the cost of one breaking minor bump now.

PRE-1.0 FRAMING: deciding between (a), (b), (c) is free pre-1.0. After 1.0 each pkix-chain major bump requires forcing every downstream consumer through migration; the cost compounds with the workspace's "RFC 5280 done right from the start" goal.

Filed as priority 1 because the lock-in shape is wider than typical for this kind of finding (four upstream crates, not just one); and because PKIX-2l0v.1 (serde derives) already widens the contract footprint by gating serde impl through the same module path.
title: pub use of entire upstream crate modules (pkix_aia, pkix_path, pkix_revocation, pkix_identity) locks pkix-chain to every upstream change
